newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl sees good result in talks with Bundesbank.
newsitem.headline: Kohl sees good result in talks with Bundesbank.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Wednesday that his government would reach a good result with the Bundesbank on talks to revalue the central bank's official reserves.
Speaking to the lower house of parliament, Kohl said talks between Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer were calm and he expected a result agreeable to both sides.

Waigel and Tietmeyer met on Tuesday to strike a compromise on Bonn's plans to revalue the Bundesbank's gold and currency reserves in an attempt to increase the central bank's profits which could be used for paying down Germany's debts.

Bonn had originally hoped to revalue the assets and transfer the profits to the federal government this year, but the Bundesbank rejected the scheme as an attack on its independence and a threat to the stability of the euro.
Government officials on Tuesday said they had struck a compromise with the central bank that would not see the profits sent to Bonn until next year.
That would be too late to help Germany qualify for monetary union. Countries hoping to join monetary union must reduce budget deficits to three percent of gross domestic product by the end of 1997.
